#data research
I am researching a federal dataset. Find out everything you can about this dataset, such as who publishes it, under what authority or mandate, its history, its typical users, and its benefits to the public. Be sure your research comprehensively covers each of those perspectives, as well as any others that you discover or seem useful. I believe this is accurate information, but please check:

Dataset title: Annual Business Survey (ABS)
Description: The Annual Business Survey (ABS) measures business owner demographics, research and development (R&D), innovation, and other topics of interest among businesses in the United States. The Business Enterprise Research and Development (BERD) Survey was integrated into the ABS in 2025. The ABS is a joint statistical project between the National Center for Science and Engineering Statistics (NCSES) within the U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF) and the U.S. Census Bureau.

Return a complete report on everything that a preservationist, data librarian, data scientist, or policy activist might want to know about this data.
prompts.assessment:
# Dataset risk assessment
I would like your help in assessing the likelihood that this data will be changed or removed from its primary location, and that users will no longer be able to access accurate and reliable copies of it, based on the rubric below.

## Sources for context
To help assess the rubric categories, perform additional research on the data, the agency, the data's topics and typical users, covering topics such as proposed regulatory or funding changes, recent news, and political commentary. Use whatever resources you find useful, including the Federal Register (https://www.federalregister.gov) and the federal staffing tracker at https://usajobs-tracker.abigailhaddad.com.

## Rubric
This rubric is divided up into categories. Each category is divided up into risk levels. In your output, please select the appropriate risk level for each category based on your research.

### Historical Data Availability
- Gone: Data files prior to the current year or cycle are no longer publicly available.
- High Risk: Some data files prior to the current year or cycle are removed.
- Moderate Risk: Some data elements that exist in the dataset prior to the current year or cycle are removed.
- No Known Issue: Data prior to the current year or cycle remain accessible with no known alterations.

### Future Data Availability
- Gone: Data collection and publication has been terminated.
- High Risk: Statutory publication deadline missed and/or collection or publication skipped and/or ICR expired for more than one year.
- Moderate Risk: Typical or intended publication date missed and/or collection or publication delayed; ICR expired up to one year.
- No Known Issue: Data published on time or as expected and ICR active or renewed before expiration.

### Data Quality
- Gone: Data collection and publication has been terminated.
- High Risk: Reductions in granularity, timeliness, or frequency.
- Moderate Risk: Potential or emerging risk to granularity, timeliness, or frequency.
- No Known Issue: Maintained or improved granularity, timeliness, or frequency.

### Statutory Context
- Gone: N/A
- High Risk: Statutory authorization is vague and/or there are alternative data collections that could serve as substitutes and/or no known programmatic use.
- Moderate Risk: Not explicitly required by statute but required for the implementation of a state or federal program, and there are no alternative data collections that could serve as substitutes.
- No Known Issue: Statutorily required and/or statutory authorization is explicitly named and it is clear what has to be collected, and there aren't alternative data collections that could serve as substitutes and/or required for implementation of a federal program.

### Staffing and Funding
- Gone: All of the staff in the division or agency are gone and/or all funding has been terminated.
- High Risk: 40% or more of staff lost, and/or 1,000 or more staff lost, and/or budget cut by 20% or more, and/or leadership removed.
- Moderate Risk: 10–39% of staff lost, and/or 500–999 staff lost, and/or budget cut by 10–19%, and/or threatened change in leadership.
- No Known Issue: Less than 10% of staff lost and less than 10% of budget cut and no known change in leadership.

### Policy
- Gone: Data collection and publication has been terminated.
- High Risk: Presidential Action-driven information collection request (ICR); negative policy note on site; other significant changes in accordance with Administration priorities.
- Moderate Risk: Proposed or pending changes; statements by administration officials suggesting a change is being considered or planned.
- No Known Issue: No notable changes since January 2025 affecting what data is collected and published.

For each category, concisely list the evidence and supporting sources that would support each risk level. Then indicate which risk level you find most appropriate and why.

Conclude with a simple summary of risk levels:
Historical Data Availability: <level>
Future Data Availability: <level>
Data Quality: <level>
Statutory Context: <level>
Staffing and Funding: <level>
Policy: <level>

[Federal Register Volume 90, Number 167 (Tuesday, September 2, 2025)]
[Notices]
[Pages 42382-42384]
From the Federal Register Online via the Government Publishing Office [www.gpo.gov]
[FR Doc No: 2025-16777]


=======================================================================
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE

Census Bureau


Agency Information Collection Activities; Submission to the 
Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for Review and Approval; Comment 
Request; Annual Business Survey

AGENCY: U.S. Census Bureau, Commerce.

ACTION: Notice of information collection, request for comment.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

SUMMARY: The Department of Commerce, in accordance with the Paperwork 
Reduction Act (PRA) of 1995, invites the general public and other 
Federal agencies to comment on proposed, and continuing information 
collections, which helps us assess the impact of our information 
collection requirements and minimize the public's reporting burden. The 
purpose of this notice is to allow for 60 days of public comment on the 
proposed revision to the Annual Business Survey prior to the submission 
of this information collection request (ICR) to OMB for approval.

DATES: To ensure consideration, comments regarding this proposed 
information collection must be received on or before November 3, 2025.

ADDRESSES: Interested persons are invited to submit written comments by 
email to [email protected]. Please reference Annual Business 
Survey in the subject line of your comments. You may also submit 
comments, identified by Docket Number USBC-2025-0104, to the Federal e-
Rulemaking Portal: http://www.regulations.gov. All comments received 
are part of the public record. No comments will be posted to http://www.regulations.gov for public viewing until after the comment period 
has closed. Comments will generally be posted without change. All 
Personally Identifiable Information (for example,

[[Page 42383]]

name and address) voluntarily submitted by the commenter may be 
publicly accessible. Do not submit Confidential Business Information or 
otherwise sensitive or protected information. You may submit 
attachments to electronic comments in Microsoft Word, Excel, or Adobe 
PDF file formats.

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: Requests for additional information or 
specific questions related to collection activities should be directed 
to Aneta Erdie, Assistant Division Chief, Governments and Business 
Owners Programs, by phone at 301-763-4841, or by email at 
[email protected].

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:

I. Abstract

    In an effort to improve the measurement of business dynamics in the 
United States, the Census Bureau is conducting the Annual Business 
Survey (ABS). The ABS combines Census Bureau firm-level collections to 
reduce respondent burden, increase data quality, reduce operational 
costs, and operate more efficiently. The ABS provides information on 
measures of research and development (R&D) as well as business and 
owner characteristics by sex, ethnicity, race, and veteran status. The 
ABS is co-sponsored by the National Center for Science and Engineering 
Statistics (NCSES) within the U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF) 
and conducted by the Census Bureau.
    Starting in 2026, the Business Enterprise Research and Development 
survey (BERD) (OMB number 0607-0912) will be merged onto the ABS. This 
merger will result in an expanded collection of R&D on the ABS to 
include R&D from all in scope employer businesses and nonprofit 
organizations. This change comes as an effort to reduce respondent 
burden and streamline collections based on respondent feedback. 
Additionally, preliminary findings from an external assessment of the 
feasibility of merging the ABS and BERD indicated that it would not 
increase burden on respondents, although burden may change based on 
other selected content for the survey. The new merged ABS content will 
be cognitively tested and will focus on business topics such as R&D, 
innovation, and technology, as well as other business and owner 
characteristics. In line with Office of Science and Technology Policy 
recommendations, two questions regarding technology have been modified 
to also collect use and funding of cybersecurity technology and nuclear 
technology. These modifications have undergone expert review.
    The ABS will sample 230,000 businesses and nonprofit organizations 
(222,000 employer business; 8,000 nonprofit organizations). The ABS 
includes all nonfarm employer businesses filing Internal Revenue 
Service (IRS) tax forms as individual proprietorships, partnerships, or 
any other type of corporation, with receipts of $1,000 or more. The 
employer sample will yield national and state R&D estimates for 
employer businesses as well as summary-level estimates for women-, 
minority-, and veteran-owned businesses at the 2-digit NAICS, U.S., 
state, counties and MSA levels. The Census Bureau selects some 
companies with certainty. All certainty cases are sure to be selected 
and represent only themselves. Also included are nonprofit 
organizations to measure their research activities. The ABS samples 
approximately 8,000 nonprofit organizations who are required to 
complete IRS form 990. The nonprofit sample will yield national 
estimates of R&D performance within the nonprofit sector. Of note, 
nonprofit organizations will only see questions relating to research 
activities and will not be asked any questions relating to owner 
demographics.
    The ABS is designed to incorporate new content each survey year 
based on topics of relevance. Each year new questions are submitted to 
the OMB for approval.
    The ABS collects the following information from employer 
businesses:
     Sex, ethnicity, race, veteran status, and other owner 
characteristics from the principal owner(s) of the business.
     Company information including, worldwide sales, domestic 
sales, number of employees, and business ownership from all employer 
businesses in the sample.
     Business characteristics from all employer businesses in 
the sample.
     Research, development, and related topics from businesses 
and nonprofits.
     Innovation related data and data on critical and emerging 
technologies (selected to be collected in 2026).
     Other potential module topics such as, cybersecurity, 
technology, intellectual property and technology transfer, and 
financing.

II. Method of Collection

    The ABS is primarily collected electronically using a web-based 
questionnaire. Those selected for the survey receive an initial letter 
informing the respondents of their requirement to complete the survey 
as well as instructions on accessing the survey. There will be pre-
notice contact for respondents who were previously in BERD informing 
the respondents of the consolidation of collections. Responses will be 
due approximately 30 days from initial mailing. Respondents will also 
receive a due date reminder approximately one week before responses are 
due. The Census Bureau plans to conduct two follow-up mailings and 
optional follow-ups if deemed necessary based on check-in. The Census 
Bureau may also plan to conduct an email follow-up to select 
nonrespondents reminding them to submit their report in the electronic 
instrument. Response data will be processed as they are received. Upon 
the close of the collection period, data processing will continue, and 
records will be edited, reviewed, tabulated, and released publicly.

III. Data

    OMB Control Number: 0607-1004.
    Form Number(s): ABS-1.
    Type of Review: Regular submission, Request for a Revision of a 
Currently Approved Collection.
    Affected Public: Businesses or other for-profit organizations 
(large and small employer businesses), nonprofit organizations.
    Estimated Number of Respondents: 230,000.
    Estimated Time per Response: The average ABS respondent will take 
45 minutes to respond; Respondents that would have previously reported 
R&D on the BERD survey will take an average of 2 hours and 37 minutes 
to respond; Nonprofit organizations will take an average of 38 minutes 
to respond.
    Estimated Total Annual Burden Hours: 295,858.
    Estimated Total Annual Cost to Public: $0. (This is not the cost of 
respondents' time, but the indirect costs respondents may incur for 
such things as purchases of specialized software or hardware needed to 
report, or expenditures for accounting or records maintenance services 
required specifically by the collection.)
    Respondent's Obligation: Mandatory.
    Legal Authority: Title 13, United States Code, Sections 8(b), 131, 
and 182; Title 42, United States Code, Section 1861-76 (National 
Science Foundation Act of 1950, as amended); and Section 505 within the 
America COMPETES Reauthorization Act of 2010 authorize this collection. 
Sections 224 and 225 of Title 13, United States Code, require response 
from sampled firms.

IV. Request for Comments

    We are soliciting public comments to permit the Department/Bureau 
to: (a)

[[Page 42384]]

Evaluate whether the proposed information collection is necessary for 
the proper functions of the Department, including whether the 
information will have practical utility; (b) Evaluate the accuracy of 
our estimate of the time and cost burden for this proposed collection, 
including the validity of the methodology and assumptions used; (c) 
Evaluate ways to enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the 
information to be collected; and (d) Minimize the reporting burden on 
those who are to respond, including the use of automated collection 
techniques or other forms of information technology.
    Comments that you submit in response to this notice are a matter of 
public record. We will include, or summarize, each comment in our 
request to OMB to approve this ICR. Before including your address, 
phone number, email address, or other personal identifying information 
in your comment, you should be aware that your entire comment--
including your personal identifying information--may be made publicly 
available at any time. While you may ask us in your comment to withhold 
your personal identifying information from public review, we cannot 
guarantee that we will be able to do so.

Sheleen Dumas,
Departmental PRA Compliance Officer, Office of the Under Secretary for 
Economic Affairs, Commerce Department.
[FR Doc. 2025-16777 Filed 8-29-25; 8:45 am]

#data research
I am researching a federal dataset. Find out everything you can about this dataset, such as who publishes it, under what authority or mandate, its history, its typical users, and its benefits to the public. Be sure your research comprehensively covers each of those perspectives, as well as any others that you discover or seem useful. I believe this is accurate information, but please check:

Dataset title: Annual Business Survey (ABS)
Description: The Annual Business Survey (ABS) measures business owner demographics, research and development (R&D), innovation, and other topics of interest among businesses in the United States. The Business Enterprise Research and Development (BERD) Survey was integrated into the ABS in 2025. The ABS is a joint statistical project between the National Center for Science and Engineering Statistics (NCSES) within the U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF) and the U.S. Census Bureau.

Return a complete report on everything that a preservationist, data librarian, data scientist, or policy activist might want to know about this data.

# Annual Business Survey (ABS): Research Report

## 1. Is your description accurate?

Mostly, yes. Two details need correcting or adding.

| Claim | Verdict | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Measures business owner demographics, R&D, innovation, and other topics | ✅ Accurate | This matches the Census Bureau's ABS landing page. Newer official text words it slightly differently: "business demographics, research and development (R&D), innovation, and critical and emerging technologies." |
| Joint project of NCSES (within NSF) and the Census Bureau | ✅ Accurate | NCSES cosponsors the survey. Census conducts it: it collects, processes and publishes the data. |
| "BERD was integrated into the ABS in 2025" | ⚠️ Partly accurate | "2025" is right only as the **data reference year**. The merge was proposed in a Federal Register notice on September 2, 2025, and OMB approved it on May 15, 2026. The first combined collection was mailed in **May 2026** and covers reference year 2025. The Census BERD page says BERD "was discontinued after the 2024 survey year." Federal Register wording: "Starting in 2026, the Business Enterprise Research and Development survey (BERD) (OMB number 0607-0912) will be merged onto the ABS." |

**Naming warning.** Until now the ABS was named by the year it was collected. The "2024 ABS" covers 2023, for example. Starting with the 2026 collection, the survey is named by the year the data describe, so the 2026 collection is the "ABS Reference Year 2025." That means two different things can be called "2025 ABS":
- the survey collected in 2025, which covers 2024 (its "First Look" tables on business credit are already out), and
- the survey collected in 2026, which covers 2025.

Census says releases already published will not be renamed. Cataloguers should record both the collection year and the reference year.

## 2. Key facts

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Title | Annual Business Survey (ABS) |
| Conducted by | U.S. Census Bureau (Department of Commerce) |
| Cosponsor | National Center for Science and Engineering Statistics (NCSES), U.S. National Science Foundation |
| OMB control number | 0607-1004 (form ABS-1). The approval cited in the 2024 cycle expires May 31, 2027. A revision for the merged survey was approved May 15, 2026. |
| Frequency | Annual. A much larger "benchmark" sample is drawn every 5 years. |
| First collection | 2018, covering 2017 |
| Unit of observation | The firm or company, not individual establishments. One report per firm. |
| Who must answer | Response is **mandatory** (13 U.S.C. §§ 224–225) |
| Confidentiality | Title 13 § 9 and Title 26 (tax data) |
| Status | Active |

## 3. Legal authority

- **Title 13, U.S. Code, §§ 8(b), 131 and 182.** Census authority for economic censuses and surveys, and for doing statistical work on behalf of other agencies.
- **Title 42, U.S. Code, §§ 1861–76.** The National Science Foundation Act of 1950, as amended.
- **Section 505 of the America COMPETES Reauthorization Act of 2010.** This establishes NCSES and its mandate to collect data on R&D and the science and engineering enterprise.
- **Title 13, §§ 224–225.** These make a response required.
- **Federal Cybersecurity Enhancement Act of 2015.** The data are protected through system screening under this law.
- **OMB's 2026 terms of clearance:**
  - Census must give all collected data to NCSES on request.
  - Census needs NCSES's written approval before any future revision.
  - All data assets must be catalogued in the agency's data inventory, as the Evidence Act of 2018 and OMB memo M-25-05 require.

## 4. History

| Year | Event |
|---|---|
| 1953 | NCSES and its predecessors begin cosponsoring an annual business R&D survey. It was later called SIRD (1953–2007), then BRDIS (2008–16), then BRDS (2017–18), then BERD (from 2019). |
| 1972 | The **Survey of Business Owners (SBO)** begins. It ran every 5 years as part of the Economic Census and covered owner sex, ethnicity, race and veteran status. |
| 2014–2016 | The **Annual Survey of Entrepreneurs (ASE)** gives yearly updates between SBO years. |
| 2016 | **BRDI-M**, the R&D and innovation survey for microbusinesses (1–9 employees), is fielded once. |
| 2017 | Federal Register notices propose the ABS. It replaces the SBO for employer firms, the ASE, BRDI-M, and the innovation section of BRDIS. |
| 2018 | First ABS, covering 2017, with about 850,000 firms. It added a technology module (AI, cloud, robotics). Response rate was about 69%, as reported in an NBER paper. |
| 2019–2022 | Annual samples of about 300,000. A module on business characteristics starts with the 2021 cycle (technology, financing, COVID-19 effects). |
| 2023 ABS (covers 2022) | Second benchmark year: about 850,000 employer firms plus about 8,000 nonprofits, which are asked only about R&D. |
| 2024 ABS (covers 2023) | About 330,000 firms sampled, mailed July 2024, response rate 64%. Released November 20, 2025, with congressional-district estimates for the first time. NCSES released microbusiness R&D results on August 17, 2026. |
| 2025 | Federal Register notice (September 2) proposes merging BERD into the ABS and adding questions on cybersecurity and nuclear technology, following White House science office (OSTP) recommendations. |
| 2026 | OMB approves the merge (May 15). The first combined survey (covers 2025) is mailed in May. Planned sample: 230,000 (222,000 employer firms and 8,000 nonprofits). BERD will no longer be fielded on its own. |

Owner demographics for businesses with no employees now come from a separate product, **Nonemployer Statistics by Demographics (NES-D)**, which is built from administrative records. Census publishes it alongside the ABS.

## 5. Scope, design and methods

**Who is covered.** Nonfarm employer businesses with receipts of $1,000 or more that file IRS forms as sole proprietorships, partnerships or corporations. That is about 5.6–5.9 million firms. Excluded industries:
- crop and animal production
- rail transportation
- Postal Service
- central banks
- funds and trusts
- notaries
- religious, civic and similar organizations
- private households
- public administration

**Sampling frame.** Built from the Census Business Register (tax returns plus Economic Census data), using data from the year before the reference year.

**How the sample is drawn.**
- The sample is divided into groups by state, industry and likely owner race, ethnicity or sex. To estimate those owner traits before sampling, Census links owners to:
  - the 2000 and 2010 censuses,
  - the American Community Survey (2005–22),
  - the Social Security Numident file,

  using IRS K-1 forms and a protected identification key.
- Some firms are always included: those with 500 or more employees, firms above size cutoffs, small firms known to do R&D, and firms in the BERD sample.
- The rest are sampled systematically within each group.

**Content.**
- Core questions:
  - percentage owned, plus sex, ethnicity, race and veteran status for up to four owners
  - other owner traits such as age and education
  - business characteristics
  - R&D for firms with 1–9 employees (and, from the 2025 reference year, all R&D content formerly on BERD)
- Rotating modules have covered:
  - innovation
  - technology and AI
  - intellectual property
  - financing and credit
  - management practices
  - manufacturing
  - cybersecurity
  - COVID-19

**How firms are classified.** A firm counts as women-, minority- or veteran-owned if that group holds 51% or more of it. Firms owned 50/50 are tabulated separately.

**Data quality (2024 ABS):**
- **Response:** 63–64% of firms responded; 63% of firms eligible for the R&D module responded.
- **Imputation (filling in missing answers):** Missing demographics come from earlier ABS answers, the 2010 census or the ACS, or are copied from similar responding firms. Imputed values make up about 14.4% of the firm-count estimates and 31.2% of the receipts estimates.
- **Owner-characteristics tables:** These are not adjusted for nonresponse. They describe owners of responding firms only (about 54.6% of classifiable firms).
- **Disclosure avoidance:** Census adds random noise to the data before tabulating. Most cells change by a few percent at most. Cells with relative standard error of 50% or more are suppressed.

**Respondent burden.**
- 2023 notice: 58 minutes per employer firm.
- 2026 merged survey:
  - 45 minutes on average
  - 2 hours 37 minutes for firms that used to report on BERD
  - 38 minutes for nonprofits
  - about 296,000 burden hours in total

## 7. Who uses it

The official needs-and-uses statements and the research record name these users:
- **Federal agencies:**
  - Small-business and minority-business programs, which use the data to assess needs, allocate resources, and plan and evaluate programs.
  - The Bureau of Economic Analysis, which uses the R&D data in the national accounts.
  - NSF and the National Science Board, through *Science and Engineering Indicators*.
  - OSTP, for critical and emerging technology priorities.
- **State and local governments and economic developers,** who compare business ownership and R&D across states, metros, counties and now congressional districts.
- **Congress,** for district-level business profiles.
- **Academic researchers,** through the microdata. A well-known example is McElheran, Brynjolfsson et al., "AI Adoption in America" (NBER w31788), which used the 2018 ABS and found that fewer than 6% of firms used AI.
- **Industry associations, chambers of commerce, lenders and businesses,** for market analysis and comparing themselves with peers.
- **Advocacy groups** for women, minority, veteran, rural and other business owners.
- **International comparisons:** innovation measures follow the OECD and Eurostat Oslo Manual, and the BERD name was chosen to match international usage.

## 8. Benefits to the public

- It is the **only large, recurring federal source of owner demographics for employer firms.** It supports evidence on gaps in entrepreneurship and access to capital.
- It is the **main source of R&D statistics for microbusinesses** (1–9 employees). From the 2025 reference year it is also the main vehicle for all business R&D statistics. Businesses and nonprofits together account for about 75% of U.S. R&D spending.
- It tracks **how technology spreads** through the economy (AI, robotics, cloud, cybersecurity) and how firms innovate.
- **Respondents are asked less often.** Several surveys were merged into one, and BERD is now folded in too.
- All tables and the API are **free to use**.

## 9. Recent changes and issues for policy watchers

1. **BERD merge.** Census and NCSES justify it as raising data quality, reducing burden and saving money. The questions had to change and were cognitively tested. **Risk:** the long R&D series dating to 1953 may have a break between reference years 2024 and 2025. Watch the comparability notes.
2. **Smaller sample.**
   - 2024 ABS: 330,000 sampled (about 300,000 is the usual non-benchmark size).
   - Merged survey: 230,000 planned, which must now also carry the R&D content.
   - The 2023 notice described the benchmark as recurring every five years. The 2026 notice I reviewed does not say whether a benchmark of about 850,000 is still planned for the next cycle due (2028, covering 2027).
   - A smaller sample means less reliable estimates for small groups and small areas.
3. **Sexual orientation and gender identity (SOGI) questions.** In 2025 Census ran cognitive interviews testing LGBTQ+ owner questions for the ABS. A March 2026 Census Project post by a researcher at the Movement Advancement Project says these questions "were removed" from the ABS after Executive Order 14168. The post calls the ABS the only nationally representative federal source on LGBTQ-owned employer firms. I could not confirm from primary sources whether SOGI items were ever published in ABS data or were only tested and planned.
4. **Wording drift.** Newer documents say "business demographics" rather than "business owner demographics," and list "critical and emerging technologies" as a core topic. The owner sex, race, ethnicity and veteran items still appear in the 2026 content list.
5. **Funding pressure on NCSES.** The FY2026 President's Budget asks $44.0 million for NCSES, down from $74.07 million in FY2024 (−40.6%). The American Statistical Association's *The Nation's Data at Risk* (2025) flags staffing losses and an office relocation.
6. **Ways to comment.** Federal Register notices under OMB 0607-1004 (docket USBC-2025-0104 for the 2025 round), reginfo.gov, and Census's annual "Current Mandatory Business Surveys" notice.

# ABS Risk Assessment: how likely the data are to be changed, lost or degraded

The biggest risks are staffing and funding at both agencies that run the survey, and the administration's policy changes to what the survey asks. The past data look safe and collection is continuing. The pressure shows up in a smaller sample and in topics being added or dropped to match administration priorities.

## 1. Historical Data Availability

**Evidence for No Known Issue**
- Census still lists data for every survey year from 2018 to 2024: published tables, the data.census.gov tables, and the API for each year (census.gov/data/developers/data-sets/abs.html). Benchmark-year county and economic-place tables for 2018 and 2023 are still there.
- The NCSES survey pages, its earlier-cycle tables and the questionnaires are still up. The 2024 ABS microbusiness R&D tables (NSF 26-321) were added in August 2026.
- Census says releases already published "will not have the year and name change." That is a renaming of future releases, not a change to past data.
- The pages of the standalone BERD survey, now discontinued, are still up.

**Evidence for higher risk**
- I found no reports of ABS files or variables being removed.
- The LGBTQ+ owner questions (sexual orientation and gender identity, "SOGI") were dropped from the survey, but they were apparently never published. Nothing already released was taken down.
- One thing to watch: an API key is now required, and the BERD pages are frozen. Neither is a removal.

**Rating: No Known Issue.** Everything published from earlier years is still available and unchanged, as far as I can find.

## 2. Future Data Availability

**Evidence for No Known Issue**
- OMB approved the survey's renewal and revision on May 15, 2026 (reginfo.gov ICR 202602-0607-001). The earlier approval ran to May 31, 2027, so it never lapsed.
- The survey collected in 2025 (covering 2024) was fielded, and its "First Look" tables are out.
- The first combined ABS-plus-BERD survey (covering 2025) was mailed in May 2026.
- The 2024 ABS (covering 2023) came out November 20, 2025. That is about 23 months after the reference year, in line with earlier cycles, even with the October–November 2025 government shutdown.

**Evidence for Moderate Risk**
- NCSES's microbusiness R&D tables for 2023 did not appear until August 17, 2026, nearly a year after Census's release. I could not confirm a promised date, so I can't say a deadline was missed.
- BERD stopped as a separate collection after the 2024 survey year. The R&D series continues only through the combined ABS.

**Rating: No Known Issue,** close to Moderate. The OMB approval is current, nothing has been skipped, and releases are roughly on their usual schedule. A delay in the full release covering 2024 would move this to Moderate.

## 3. Data Quality

**Evidence for High or Moderate Risk**
- The sample is shrinking just as the survey takes on more:
  - 2024 ABS: 330,000 firms.
  - Combined survey: 230,000 (222,000 businesses and 8,000 nonprofits), which must now also carry all the R&D content formerly on BERD.
  - The usual sample for non-benchmark years had been about 300,000.
- The Federal Register notice of September 2, 2025 (2025-16777) doesn't say whether the five-year benchmark sample of about 850,000 will still happen in the cycle due next (covering 2027).
- A smaller sample means less reliable estimates for small owner groups and small areas.
- The 2024 ABS already had imputed values in about 31% of receipts estimates and a 64% response rate.
- Merging BERD into the ABS changed the questions, so the R&D series dating to 1953 may break between reference years 2024 and 2025.

**Evidence for No Known Issue**
- The 2025 notice still promises:
  - national and state R&D estimates,
  - summary-level estimates for women-, minority- and veteran-owned businesses at the U.S., state, county and metro levels,
  - nonprofit R&D estimates.
- The 2024 ABS added congressional-district tables for the first time.
- Frequency is still annual, and releases have not slowed.

**Rating: Moderate Risk.** Geographic detail and frequency have held so far, and have even improved. But the much smaller sample, carrying more content, puts their reliability at risk going forward.

## 4. Statutory Context

**Evidence for No Known Issue**
- The legal authorities are named explicitly:
  - Title 13 §§ 8(b), 131 and 182 for Census.
  - 42 U.S.C. §§ 1861–76 (the NSF Act).
  - Section 505 of the America COMPETES Reauthorization Act of 2010. This requires NCSES to collect data on R&D and the science and engineering enterprise.
  - Title 13 §§ 224–225 make response mandatory.
- Now that BERD has been folded in, the ABS is the only federal source of business R&D statistics. Business R&D accounts for most U.S. R&D spending.
  - The Bureau of Economic Analysis uses these statistics in GDP's intellectual-property accounts.
  - They also feed the National Science Board's congressionally required *Science and Engineering Indicators*.
- Nothing else measures owner demographics for employer firms. NES-D covers only businesses with no employees.

**Evidence for Moderate or High Risk**
- No statute names "the ABS." It rests on general Title 13 authority.
- The demographic content traces to executive orders and program needs rather than an explicit statutory requirement:
  - minority-business orders such as EO 11625,
  - women's business enterprise orders,
  - possibly the Women's Business Ownership Act of 1988. I have not confirmed this one.
- A main user of that content, the Minority Business Development Agency, was ordered cut back to its legal minimum by EO 14238 in March 2025.

**Rating: No Known Issue,** with a caveat. The R&D content is clearly required by statute, and nothing else could replace it. The demographic content is the weaker part legally. It is the most exposed if the survey is narrowed.

## 5. Staffing and Funding

**Evidence for High Risk**
- **NCSES budget:** The FY2026 President's Budget asks $44.0 million, down from $74.07 million in FY2024 (−40.6%). Sources: the NSF FY26 budget request and the American Statistical Association's *The Nation's Data at Risk* (2025). I did not confirm the final enacted FY26 amount; check it.
- **NSF overall:**
  - NSF's order to restructure its workforce (memo OD 25-35, May 2025) eliminated 84 of 143 senior executive positions and cut temporary staff from 368 to about 70.
  - In-person work was required, and NCSES was ordered to move offices.
  - The ASA reports NCSES's FY25–26 staffing was not made public. Even before these cuts, NCSES had "severe staffing constraints."
- **Census:**
  - About 1,300–1,500 staff left through deferred resignation and early retirement (AFGE local, AP, Bloomberg Law). That is about 15% of staff since FY24, according to the ASA.
  - About 100 more received layoff notices during the shutdown.
  - The FY26 request cuts staffing for periodic censuses and programs by 27%.
- **Leadership:**
  - Census Director Santos resigned in February 2025.
  - A political appointee, George Cook, became acting director in September 2025.
  - The NSF director also resigned in 2025.
- **USAJobs tracker:** the page loaded without its data, and it is being archived (its data collection stopped December 31, 2025). I could not get job-posting figures for these agencies from it.

**Evidence for lower risk**
- Census's core current-surveys staffing is only 2% lower in the FY26 request.
- Collecting the survey is still paid for, and it was fielded in 2026.

**Rating: High Risk.** Census has lost more than 1,000 staff, the proposed NCSES budget cut is about 40%, and leadership has been removed or replaced at both agencies.

## 6. Policy

**Evidence for High Risk**
- **LGBTQ+ owner questions dropped.** Census cognitively tested questions on LGBTQ+ business owners in 2025. According to The Census Project, in a post by the Movement Advancement Project's data policy advisor (March 2026), they were removed after **EO 14168**, the executive order on "gender ideology." **Evidence for lower risk**
- The questions on owner sex, race, ethnicity and veteran status are kept in the 2026 content, and the survey stays mandatory and annual.
- I found no negative policy note on the Census or NCSES pages.

**Rating: High Risk.** Content was removed under an executive order, and other content was added at the White House science office's direction. Both are significant changes in line with administration priorities.
